name: # The rows that LEFT divergent.tsv: each a divergence that was repaired,
# with the one answer every runtime gives since. The register proves a
# split is live. This file proves it stays closed, through the same
# probes and the same runners, ts/test/divergent.test.js,
# go/divergent_test.go and rs/tests/divergent_spec_test.rs, so a row
# moves here from the register by dropping two of its three runtime
# columns and its justification. FIVE tab-separated columns:
#   name      the register's name, kept, so the DIVERGENCE.md entry under
#             "Repaired, and what replaced them" can still cite it
#   probe     `lex` or `spec`, as divergent.tsv defines them
#   arg       the probe's arguments, as divergent.tsv spells them
#   input     the source text
#   expected  what EVERY runtime produces since the repair
# A `# @repaired:` line names the DIVERGENCE.md entry its rows came from.
# That entry must no longer be a `### ` heading there and must still be
# mentioned under "Repaired": go/divergent_test.go checks both, and that
# no name here is also a row name in divergent.tsv. A row that fails here
# is a repaired divergence coming back. It belongs in divergent.tsv again,
# with its entry, not in an edit to this column.
# The escapes and rendering rules of divergent.tsv apply unchanged: \n,
# \r and \t are decoded in every column, a control character inside a
# JSON `arg` is spelled \uXXXX, and a rendered `src` or value cannot hold
# a tab, newline or carriage return.
# @repaired: A row counted at a raw U+2028 or U+2029 inside a string in Rust
# Under json5's row characters, LF, U+2028 and U+2029, a line character
# inside a single-line string is body: a column, never a row, and not
# `unprintable` when it is in `line.chars` as well. Rust counted a row
# for any row character its cursor stepped over, string body or not, and
# refused any line character inside a single-line string. The last three
# rows are neighbours the same loop decided: a row character outside
# `line.chars` inside a multi-line string, a CR inside a multi-line
# string, and that CR's CRLF control.
string-row-char-control
string-raw-ls
string-raw-ps
string-raw-ls-line-char
string-raw-ps-line-char
string-raw-ls-value
string-raw-ls-then-row
string-raw-nel
string-multi-row-char-only
string-multi-cr
string-multi-crlf-control
# @repaired: No row counted at a raw U+2028 or U+2029 inside a multi-line string in Go
# Under json5's line configuration, with the double quote in
# `string.multiChars`, a raw line character inside a multi-line string
# counts a row at any code point, LF, U+2028, U+2029 and a Latin-1
# U+0085 alike. Go tested the line and row sets only below code point
# 32, and TypeScript's own table only below 32 inside its 256 entries.
string-multi-row-char-control
string-multi-raw-ls
string-multi-raw-ps
string-multi-raw-ls-ps
string-multi-raw-nel
string-multi-raw-ls-value
# @repaired: An escaped non-ASCII character read as one byte in Go
# The character after the escape character counts one column whatever
# its UTF-8 width, and a `string.escape` mapping of a non-ASCII character
# applies. Go read one byte and stepped one byte, so the column ran ahead
# by the width minus one and the mapping was never found. The astral
# case is not here: `"\😀" y` puts `y` at 7 in TypeScript, two UTF-16
# units, and 6 in Go and Rust, the split under "Column positions for
# astral characters".
escape-ascii-control
escape-two-byte
escape-three-byte
escape-two-byte-value
escape-map-ascii-control
escape-map-two-byte
escape-map-three-byte
